title: Playing at Tulane University around 1910
summary: Garland remembers Tulane as already old, playing parties and dances there; Happy Bolton singing private songs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. Tell me about the place where I work. What was it like to go up to Tulane University in 1910?
Tulane University?
Was it new then or old?

No, it was old. I'll tell you about the Tulane University. It was old. I guess it's been remodeled six or seven times since I, since that time. This was a big place, university, Tulane University. Football games, you know, and all like that.
Well, you played up there, huh?
I played there, yeah.
What kind of a deal would that be you were playing? Would it be a dance or just a party or what?
No, I played, yeah, party. Yeah. Dance, you know.
Mm-hmm. Yeah. You don't remember the old gym up there, do you?
No, I don't remember nothing.
That's where Joe Oliver used to play. In the gym up there.
Well, yeah, I know that's where we played too, you said, do I remember. I don't remember, I remember playing it.
I think Happy Bolton was on drums with Joe Oliver. Jim, that might have been after your time.
Might have been.

Because, do you know Johnny Hyman, Johnny Wiggs? He used to be a student around, you know, and he'd go there. And he'd tell me about Happy Bolton singing all the songs over in the corner. Well, only the young men could listen and the ladies couldn't hear them.
Well, that was one of them private songs.
Yeah.
Back in the nightclub.
Yeah, that's what I mean.
Get over in the corner and sing.
